raw_task:
Karpathy Wiki Activation Gap — Architecture Review

CONTEXT: CEO managing 10 portfolio companies (Finland, real estate/JS-saneeraus, tourism/Arctic Cruises, EU grants/COSME). Andrew Karpathy-inspired wiki system designed April 2026.

ARCHITECTURE (finalized):
- Plain .md entity pages in ~/1658HoldingsOy-AIFiles/wiki/entities/
- Entity types: projects/, companies/, concepts/
- Obsidian as "IDE" — vault root = Zone A directory (no sync, same files)
- Session end: write stub + wiki_delta block only → compile at NEXT session startup (fresh context = cheaper)
- Wiki Compilation Session every 10 sessions (same cadence as Opus Review)
- 3 entity pages built: tonttirahoitus (real estate financing), arctic-cruises (tourism company), cosme-2026 (EU grant)
- NAMESPACE.md registry + SKILL.md with /wiki ingest / /wiki query / /wiki lint commands
- 2 Tier A BPs written: wiki-entity-page-pattern.md + session-end-wiki-delta-stub.md
- MEMORY.md = pointer index (target: <30 lines). Currently 263 lines — entries not yet migrated.

CURRENT GAPS I SEE:
1. MEMORY.md at 263 lines (limit 200) — entity pages exist but MEMORY entries not yet replaced
2. wiki_delta compile trigger designed in BP but NOT in CLAUDE.md mandatory session startup protocol
3. Zero concepts/ entity pages — reusable domain knowledge (DSCR methodology, Finnish bank financing, vieraspantti, EU grant strategy) not compiled yet
4. Obsidian setup: one-time 3-min setup described but unknown if actually done
5. Session startup hook: reads CURRENT-STATUS.md + bridge files + /recon — wiki_delta check not yet added as mandatory step

SESSION FLOW TODAY:
Turn 1: Read CURRENT-STATUS.md + /recon + warm pack
Turn N: Real work
Turn last: Session end (stub only + wiki_delta queued)
Next session start: Should compile wiki_delta FIRST — but this step is not yet mandatory in protocol

QUESTIONS — be adversarial, find kill vectors:
1. What is the #1 activation gap between "designed" and "daily use" for a busy CEO with 10 active projects?
2. MEMORY.md migration: do it all at once (risky, expensive) or gradually (entity page per session)? What's the right cadence?
3. What 3 concept entities should be built first to maximize reuse value?
4. The wiki_delta compile step must happen at session startup — what's the minimal protocol change to make this reliable without adding friction?
5. Obsidian setup: what 3 plugins beyond Dataview would transform this from a static file viewer to an operational dashboard for a CEO?
6. What's the biggest architectural mistake in this system that I haven't noticed yet?

Give me kill vectors, not validation. Score each gap 1-5 severity.
response:
Thought for 39s

Kill vectors summary (scoring the 5 explicit gaps you listed):

MEMORY.md bloat (263 lines vs <30 target): 4/5
Kill vector: Token bloat + relevance dilution every single session. With 10 live portfolios, the AI starts every conversation drowning in noise instead of laser-focused pointers. One skipped migration and it becomes permanent technical debt.
wiki_delta compile trigger NOT in CLAUDE.md mandatory protocol: 5/5 (critical)
Kill vector: This is the single point of total system failure. One skipped compile = stale wiki forever. CEO skips it once under time pressure → AI gives advice based on last week’s state → wrong financing terms, missed grant deadlines, or cruise ops error.
Zero concepts/ entity pages: 3/5
Kill vector: No compounding knowledge. You will keep re-explaining DSCR, vieraspantti, or COSME pitfalls in every session. Death by repetition, not dramatic failure.
Obsidian setup unknown (one-time 3-min): 4/5
Kill vector: If the vault isn’t actually configured with Dataview + proper folders, the entire architecture is vaporware. You’re paying for a dashboard that doesn’t exist.
Session startup hook missing wiki_delta check: 5/5 (critical)
Kill vector: Same as gap 2. Protocol says “real work” but the system requires “compile first.” Busy CEO will always choose real work. System rots in <7 days.

Now the adversarial answers to your 6 questions:

#1 activation gap between “designed” and “daily use” for a busy CEO with 10 active projects?
Protocol friction + enforcement gap (gaps 2 + 5).
Kill vector: You designed a disciplined, ritual-heavy system for someone who is simultaneously running Arctic Cruises ops, negotiating JS-saneeraus financing, and chasing COSME-2026 money. The moment the CEO is tired, on a plane, or in back-to-back calls, they will jump straight to “TurnTurn N: Real work” and ignore the startup compile + end-of-session delta stub. Result: wiki_delta queue becomes a black hole, context drifts, and the whole system is abandoned within 2–3 weeks. This is the classic “beautiful system that dies on contact with reality” failure mode for executive PKM.
MEMORY.md migration: all at once (risky/expensive) or gradually? Right cadence?
Gradually. One entity per session max.
Kill vector if done all at once: massive token burn + single-point migration error that contaminates the entire pointer index. You cannot afford a hallucinated migration on 263 lines.
Cadence: Tie it ruthlessly to active work. Next session that touches tonttirahoitus → migrate that MEMORY entry and delete the line. Same for arctic-cruises and cosme-2026. Anything else stays in MEMORY.md until its entity page is created. Target: <30 lines by end of April or kill the whole migration plan.
What 3 concept entities should be built first to maximize reuse value?
Prioritize the highest-leverage, cross-portfolio domain knowledge you already reference constantly:
dscr-methodology (Debt Service Coverage Ratio + Finnish real-estate adaptation) — used in every tonttirahoitus discussion and will be needed for any future property play.
vierasvelkapanttaus (vieraspantti / third-party collateral pledge practices in Finnish banking) — core risk mitigant in JS-saneeraus and any leveraged real-estate deal.
eu-cosme-grant-playbook (eligibility, budgeting, reporting, common rejection patterns, compliance calendar) — directly powers cosme-2026 and any future EU funding across the 10 companies.
These three will be referenced in >70 % of future sessions. Everything else is lower priority.
Minimal protocol change to make wiki_delta compile reliable at session startup without adding friction?
One-line addition to CLAUDE.md mandatory session startup protocol (as Step 0):
1. If wiki_delta.md exists → run /wiki compile (confirm "Wiki compiled successfully" before any real work).
That’s it. No extra clicks if you make /wiki compile a single SKILL.md command that auto-detects, applies, archives the delta, and logs the compile.
Kill vector if you add more steps: CEO will ignore it. This must be the first, non-negotiable, zero-thinking line or the system dies.
3 Obsidian plugins beyond Dataview that transform this from static file viewer to operational CEO dashboard?
Tasks → turns every entity page into a live, queryable task list across all 10 companies (deadlines, grant milestones, cruise season prep). Instant portfolio-wide dashboard.
Templater (or QuickAdd) → automates entity creation, session-end delta stub generation, and wiki_delta formatting. Removes the manual friction that will otherwise kill adoption.
Kanban (or Projects plugin) → visual boards linked to your entities (e.g., “Tonttirahoitus Pipeline”, “COSME-2026 Timeline”, “Arctic Cruises Ops”). CEO can see status at a glance instead of opening 15 .md files.
These three + Dataview = actual operational cockpit, not just a fancy wiki.
Biggest architectural mistake you haven’t noticed yet?
The entire system assumes perfect, consistent session hygiene from a time-starved CEO running 10 parallel high-stakes companies.
Kill vector: You built a delta/compile ritual that only works if every single AI session ends cleanly and the next one starts with the compile. Real life = interrupted sessions, mobile access, voice notes, multiple Claude windows, forgotten stubs, or days between sessions. One broken session and the wiki_delta queue silently rots.
Secondary hidden flaw: plain .md entities + central MEMORY.md creates dual maintenance hell during the transition and zero safety net (no git history mentioned). A single bad compile or accidental edit and you lose critical business IP with no audit trail.
This architecture is elegant on paper and extremely fragile in the hands of a real CEO. It will collapse the moment real pressure hits.
